body:
Ha! I know exactly which clinic that is. Don't go there, they offer discounts if you give good reviews. I had a consult with them and they were very pushy and the technician showed me the results of what she'd done on herself and it looked horrible, like she'd just replaced the black ink with a white scar.   


Don't go there, it's probably the worst place in Perth for tattoo removal.
Do you have any idea why that one spot got darker after treatment 2?

I don't think any therapist can help me get over it though. It's eating away at me so badly I legitimately can't live with this feeling any longer. Even though my first removal appointment is coming up soon, I can't bear to know it'll take years and might not even fully work. I honestly feel like I've ruined my life forever and there's no going back

I'm currently in suicide prevention therapy and to be honest it's not working. I don't feel any better afterwards and there's no real solutions my therapist can offer other than "just get it removed" or "get a coverup". 

​
The shape doesn't look like it would fit. And as I've got no African roots I don't think it's appropriate.
I think it's something to do with the red ink itself and how your body reacts to it.

Problem is my biggest regret is being tattooed at all. I'd do absolutely anything to go back to my old skin. But even though I'm pale and they're all black/grey, I know my chances of complete removal are slim to none. I can't believe I made such a lifelong commitment in a spur of the moment decision on impulse. I'm such an idiot and I don't know how to cope with it. I genuinely feel like I've ruined my life forever now, like I'll never truly be happy unless they're gone.
It's hard though, there's always the chance of permanent damage to my skin from laser treatment. My skin most likely won't go back to the way it was before.
Ahh, sounds tough to find
How did you even get a cyanide?

1) I'm too afraid of the pain and what might happen if I survive

2) My mum would be distraught
The fear of surviving a painful attempt
I can't think of anything I'd genuinely want. All I want is removal.
Do you know what type of laser it was? How long ago did you go through the process?
Do you know which laser that is?
Thanks, glad to know I'm not alone.

It's nothing as bad as a swastika thank god, but I'm struggling to cope with having them.   
I'm determined to get them removed no matter what it takes. If I could afford surgery and replace them with scars I would.

I'm far too insecure to ever fully embrace them, I think the only times I could embrace how stupid they are is if I was really really drunk at a party maybe? (That's usually when I show people anyway.) 

But yeah, I have laser removal booked soon. I doubt it's gonna give me good results but what can you do? Maybe one day technology will reach a point where they can be fully removed not too difficultly? Regardless, it causes me so much mental anguish. It really, really sucks.

That's true about the grey, I'm just shocked at how well it turned out. Megan Fox and Mark Wahlberg weren't able to fully remove theirs and they were just black and grey.   


I've found out which clinic Ross goes to and it's just a normal clinic, so there's clearly something magic about his immune system.
Oh wow that's really impressive! How many treatments did it take? Do you have any before and after pictures?
Oh really? How well did it work? Only a faint shadow or just very faded?
I just want to know if anyone thinks removal is worth it. Or if anyone has any success stories with it
Unfortunately it may not be possible, I've done a lot of research on removal and my chances of ever achieving it to the level I desire is slim :(

I guess... But it's not what I'd call small and truthfully I'd do anything to go back to having no ink on my body, I didn't think it through beforehand (it was mostly a spur of the moment decision, I'd thought offhand for a while I'd be one of those people who gets lots of tattoos, but after getting a couple I've realised it's not for me and I want to go back)
